category: no-code scraper with a desktop project builder and cloud runs

free_tier.stated: Free plan, no credit card: 200 pages per run, 5 public projects, data retention for 14 days, 200 pages of data in 40 minutes, limited support; no run count is stated, runs past the speed limit queue, and Free holds up to 100 queued runs. Data downloads as CSV (Excel) or JSON and through the REST API
free_tier.notes: a page is every content load: a new URL, a scroll that loads more content, or a click that goes to the next page of results; the allowance is per run, not per month

per_object_cap.stated: 200 pages per run on Free (10,000 on Standard, unlimited on Professional); a results file over 10 MB is not saved as CSV, only as JSON
per_object_cap.notes: the 10 MB CSV ceiling is from https://help.parsehub.com/hc/en-us/articles/115006152168-Convert-JSON-to-CSV

retention.stated: run data is kept for 14 days on Free and Standard, 30 days on Professional

egress.terms: not applicable: run data downloads as CSV or JSON

interface_detail: REST API v2 under https://www.parsehub.com/api/v2/ with an api_key parameter from the account page: start a run of a project on the ParseHub cloud, poll the run, and fetch its data as csv or json (always gzip-encoded); the desktop application for Mac, Windows and Linux builds projects by point and click
tooling: the ParseHub desktop application (Mac .dmg, Windows installer, Linux AppImage) builds projects; runs execute on ParseHub servers; the REST API starts runs and fetches data
chaining: Build a project once in the desktop application, then start runs and pull JSON over the REST API from any scheduler, since scheduling is a paid feature; Free projects are public, so their designs and run data may be shared with other users

limits.value: 200 pages per run on Free; every new URL, content-loading scroll or next-page click counts as one page
200 pages in 40 minutes on Free, 5 pages a minute; each worker scrapes up to 5 pages a minute and runs past the speed limit queue
up to 100 queued runs on Free, 100,000 on paid plans
API: 5 requests a second, queued up to 25 a second, then HTTP 429 (API reference); six concurrent connections per IP and 60 requests in any 30 seconds (help center)
run data kept 14 days on Free
5 projects on Free, all public: project designs and the data from their runs may be shared with other users

binding_note: 5 pages a minute bounds a Free account at 7,200 pages a day however many runs are queued; the 200-page run cap only forces a large crawl into many runs

identity_cost.detail: no credit card is required to sign up; the sign-up form posts a name, an email address and a password, and the sign-up code carries an email-verification screen

reliability_note: a results file over 10 MB is not saved as CSV: the CSV download comes back empty with a notice and only the JSON holds the data
confidence_note: every value is read from ParseHub's own pricing page, API reference, help center and sign-up code; the 7,200-pages-a-day ceiling is derived from the stated 200 pages in 40 minutes

notes: Confirmed as a no-code scraper with a free plan. Free runs: no run count is stated; a project can be run many times, runs past the speed limit queue, and Free holds up to 100 queued runs. Pages per run: 200 on Free (10,000 on Standard at USD 189 a month, unlimited on Professional). Export formats: CSV (opened as Excel) and JSON from the desktop application, the website or the API. The desktop application only builds projects; runs execute on ParseHub servers, so no machine has to stay on. The caveats are that Free projects are public and run data is kept 14 days.
